beginner.summary: For programmers and analysts who know Python and some linear algebra and want a framework-neutral grounding in how neural networks work. Covers tensors and shapes, perceptrons, activations, losses and maximum likelihood, gradient descent, backpropagation, the training loop, data splits and leakage, overfitting and regularisation, initialisation, normalisation, optimisers, one day on convolutional networks, embeddings, metrics, debugging and reproducible runs, with PyTorch used only as the lab vehicle, ending in a diagnosed Fashion-MNIST classifier.
prerequisites: Writes Python functions and uses NumPy arrays and pandas DataFrames
Knows vectors, matrices, derivatives and the chain rule at undergraduate level
Has a laptop with Python 3.10 or later and about 5 GB of free disk space, with a GPU optional
outcomes: Explain forward propagation, backpropagation, loss functions and gradient descent and verify them numerically
Write and debug a complete training and evaluation loop with correct data splits and metrics
Diagnose overfitting, bad initialisation and training failures using curves and statistics
Deliver a reproducible classifier study with baselines, ablations and a written diagnosis
